subtitle: A passive with no subject, and the action and the state
words.intro: In Berlin, a club door is a matter of serious philosophy. You wait in line for three hours and then a person with face tattoos looks at you for two seconds. Nobody knows why. There are no photos inside.

grammar[0].fact: German likes this sentence for signs: *Hier wird nicht geraucht*. It gives an order without anyone giving it. In the kitchen, *Jetzt wird gegessen!* is a parent’s last warning. The grammar stays polite. The tone doesn’t.

grammar[1].fact: Shop doors tell you the difference: *Wir sind geöffnet* means the result, we’re open. *Der Laden wird um acht geöffnet*: someone comes at eight and opens it. In German both end in *geöffnet*, and one tiny verb tells you if you’ve arrived too early.

document.intro: Now the opposite of a club: a real sign at a school in Küsnacht, in Switzerland. It says what is forbidden, as politely as it can. Swiss German has its own words: *parkieren* for parken, *Benützung* for Benutzung.
document.fact: Each German-speaking country has its own office German. Switzerland has *parkieren* and *das Velo*; Austria has *der Jänner* and *die Matura*. Swiss people also write *ss* for every *ß*: a letter they gave up long ago.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Turn each rule into a passive with no subject.
reading.intro: It is four on a Sunday morning in Berlin. Frau Huber has heard that nobody gets into this club, and she doesn’t like being told that. She has brought Maya, her good handbag and a thermos. There’s a queue round the block, and at the door stands a very tall man called Sven.
reading.photos[1].caption: Eine Tanzfläche im Licht. Um sechs wird das Licht angemacht.
reading.fact: A German tax court ruled in 2016 that a famous Berlin club counts as a cultural venue, which means lower tax, much like a theatre. Some clubs put a small sticker over your phone’s camera at the door. In some the party begins on Saturday night and ends on Monday.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Say it without man. Start with Hier wird …
